telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The stored E.164 'telephone' formatted for humans: the country code, a
                single space, then the national digits grouped in threes (e.g. the stored
                '+61412345678' displays as '+61 412 345 678'). Derived from the owner's own
                fields; the raw 'telephone' stays in E.164 form.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>' where REGION is the
                region code derived from the postcode (NSW/VIC/QLD, else UNKNOWN) and HASH8
                is the first 8 upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over the normalized
                (E.164) telephone concatenated with lastName. Assigned at creation.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                A single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits contained in the
                owner's customerCode. Derived from the owner's own fields.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where YY
                is the last two digits of the fiscalYear derived from the
                business-day-adjusted registrationDate (e.g. 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26').
                Derived from the owner's own fields.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26'
              readOnly: true
            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: >-
                The owner's fiscal year, formatted 'FY<YY>' where YY is the last two
                digits of the fiscal year derived from the business-day-adjusted
                registrationDate. The fiscal year starts on 1 July and is labelled by the
                calendar year in which it ends, so a registrationDate on or after 1 July
                falls in the following year's fiscal year (e.g. 1 July 2025 -> 'FY26').
                Null when no registrationDate is set. Derived from the owner's own fields.
              type: string
              example: 'FY26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by all owners in the same household. Derived
                deterministically as the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256 over
                (normalized last name + '|' + postcode), so owners with the same last
                name and postcode always share it. Always assigned.
              type: string
              example: 'HH-3F2A9C1D5E6B7A8C'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners, at the moment this owner was created,
                sharing the same firstName and lastName (compared case-insensitively).
                Fixed at creation time.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership points, assigned at creation. Starts at 0;
                add 2 when an email is present; add 1 when namesakeCount is 0; add 2 for a
                household of 3 or more; add 3 for tenure of at least one elapsed fiscal
                year. Derived from the owner's own fields.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, assigned at creation. Derived from
                membershipPoints: 1 (0-1 points), 2 (2-3), 3 (4-5), 4 (6 or more).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's region, taken from the REGION segment of the customerCode (the
                region-and-hash identity, derived from the postcode). 'UNKNOWN' when no
                region could be derived. Derived from the owner's own fields.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: >-
                The owner's IANA timezone name, derived from the locality/region via the
                fixed region-to-timezone table (NSW -> Australia/Sydney, VIC ->
                Australia/Melbourne, QLD -> Australia/Brisbane). Derived from the owner's
                own fields.
              type: string
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'

All changes compile and the app serves identical responses to baseline. Here's a summary of the preparation work.

## What I did

The project has exactly one test — `AcceptanceTest`, which is the **acceptance criteria for the upcoming `memberId` change** and was already red at baseline (NPE on the not-yet-existent `memberId` field). I left it red (implementing `memberId` is the change itself, which I was told not to do) and verified my restructuring keeps the created-owner response **byte-for-byte identical** to baseline (`customerCode` `NSW-16E6609E`, `checkDigit` `8`, `membershipNumber` `NSW-16E6609E-M27`, `fiscalYear` `FY27`). So behaviour is preserved and no previously-working behaviour regressed.

The restructuring follows this codebase's established idiom — one small `model` class per derived value / shared primitive (like `Sha256`, `Soundex`, `FiscalYear`, `CheckDigit`) — so the listed hotspots stay thin when the change lands:

1. **`model/Luhn.java`** (new) — the Luhn check-digit algorithm as a reusable primitive. `CheckDigit.of(owner)` now delegates to it. Gives the future `MemberId::luhn` (its CHK segment) a clean primitive instead of an inlined loop.

2. **`model/Hash8.java`** (new) — the HASH8 identity segment (SHA-256-first-8-upper over telephone+lastName), extracted from `AssignCustomerCode`'s private helper. Now the *same* code the future `MemberId::of` reuses (the spec calls it "the same … first-8-hex used by the region-and-hash identity"), rather than a re-implementation. `AssignCustomerCode` shrank to `region + "-" + Hash8.of(owner)`.

3. **`model/MembershipNumber.java`** (new) — the `<customerCode>-M<YY>` derivation that was **duplicated inline** in `OwnerMapper` and `AuditOwnerCreated`. Both now call `MembershipNumber.of(owner)`. This directly de-complexifies `AuditOwnerCreated::service` (now a single log call) and gives one place to change/remove when the fields unify.

4. **`FiscalYear.shortYear(LocalDate)`** (new) — the 2-digit `YY` accessor, de-duplicating the `%02d … %100` formatting shared by `FiscalYear.of` and the membership-number sites. This is exactly the FY segment the future `memberId` (`<REGION><FY><HASH8><CHK>`) needs.

## Hotspots and how each is relieved

- `MemberId::of` / `MemberId::luhn` — will assemble from clean pieces (`Locality.regionOf`, `FiscalYear.shortYear`, `Hash8.of`, `Luhn.digit`) instead of inlining hashing/Luhn/formatting.
- `AssignMemberId::deduplicate` / `existingMemberIds` — already thin; with assembly living in `Hash8`/`MemberId`, the future `service` stays a `MemberId.of` + dedup.
- `AuditOwnerCreated::service` — already reduced to one log line here.
- `Owner::getMemberId/setMemberId` — become a plain field rename (no derivation crept into accessors, since `membershipNumber`/`checkDigit` remain derived in `model/`).
- `Locality::of` — I left it untouched: its future complexity is parsing a region prefix out of the delimiter-less `memberId`, which is inherent to the *new format* and belongs to the future `MemberId` class. Relieving it now would require implementing the change.

I did **not** create a `MemberId` class or rename the `customerCode` field/DTO — those are the change itself.
